newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank sees no need to adjust key rate - paper.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank sees no need to adjust key rate - paper.

text.p: Bank of Finland director Matti Vanhala was quoted as saying on Thursday that there was no reason to adjust key interest rates.
"The situation is stable. There is no reason to change the set-up," Vanhala said according to daily Turun Sanomat.
"We do not see yet a need for any monetary policy reaction," Vanhala said, referring to the incomes settlement talks.
In summer 1995, prior to the last round of collective pay bargaining, the Bank of Finland hiked its key tender rate, warning of inflationary pressures of excessive pay rises.
Vanhala said recent views expressed by labour market leaders had been moderate, and based on those views one could not say that inflation pressures would be mounting.
He also said he did not expect the rise in construction costs to spread through the whole economy, the paper said.
The Bank of Finland's tender rate has been unchanged at 3.00 percent -- on par with the German Bundesbank's repo rate -- since October.
But although it was "nicely in line", Vanhala denied that the Finnish tender rate would directly track the German repo rate, Turun Sanomat said.

Statistics Finland on Thursday reported that Finnish consumer prices rose 1.0 percent year-on-year in April, up from 0.6 percent in March. Core inflation rose 0.1 percent year-on-year in March, down from 0.2 percent in February.
The central bank's target for underlying inflation is for a year-on-year rise of no more than about two percent on average.
